findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so the strategy provides no backpressure
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates each queue.Queue with no maxsize and submit() always returns after put(). Because SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit therefore never blocks or rejects a message, Arroyo can keep polling Kafka and accumulating decoded WorkItems, OffsetTracker entries, and queued payloads in memory whenever workers fall behind—the exact slow-consumer scenario this mode is meant to handle. This contradicts the strategy docstring's claimed natural backpressure and can OOM the consumer instead of pausing consumption.

findings.title: Failed work items are marked complete and become committable
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker catches every exception from result_processor, then its finally block calls offset_tracker.complete_offset(). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit has the same problem for grouping/submission failures at lines 317-325: it logs, adds the offset, and immediately completes it. A failed uptime result can consequently be committed as if successfully processed, with no retry or DLQ handling, despite the class docstring promising that offsets are committed only after successful processing.

findings.title: Closing one strategy shuts down the factory-shared queue pool
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ and passes that same pool to every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy it creates. Arroyo closes the old strategy when partitions are revoked and then asks the same factory for a new strategy, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() calls queue_pool.shutdown(), shutting down all queues and workers. The replacement strategy then reuses a dead pool; subsequent queue.put calls raise queue.ShutDown, which submit() catches and marks complete, so messages after a rebalance can be silently dropped and committed.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown does not drain queued work
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets worker.shutdown=True before calling Queue.shutdown(immediate=False). OrderedQueueWorker checks that flag in its while condition, so after finishing—or waking from—its current item it exits even if its queue still contains items that immediate=False was supposed to let it drain. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() also never waits for the queues to empty before shutting the pool down, so close() abandons queued work rather than completing it before Arroyo tears down the assignment.

findings.title: terminate() can commit offsets after the strategy has terminated
findings.body: terminate() sets shutdown_event but does not join commit_thread, unlike close(). _commit_loop waits for one second and then computes and calls commit_function without rechecking shutdown_event before committing, so a terminated strategy whose partitions may already have been revoked can still invoke Arroyo's commit callback after termination.

findings.title: Group assignment uses Python's randomized hash()
findings.body: get_queue_for_group() uses built-in hash(group_key), whose result for strings is randomized per Python process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed. The mapping is therefore not the consistent hashing claimed in the docstring across restarts or across consumer processes; the same subscription can move to a different worker/queue in another process, weakening the within-group ordering guarantee for results that are not confined to one process/partition assignment. A stable digest-based hash should be used instead.

findings.title: Commit scan is O(backlog) every second and holds the partition lock
findings.body: get_committable_offsets() runs every second and iterates range(start, max_offset + 1) while holding the partition lock. When one early offset is stuck, mark_committed never prunes all_offsets/outstanding, so every later offset for that partition makes the retained sets and the scanned range larger; the commit thread repeatedly rescans the whole backlog while blocking worker threads that need the same lock in add_offset()/complete_offset(). This degrades precisely under a slow-item backlog.
